attacks.unsupported_mechanism: KILLED - claimed 50 nm pores provide "absolute physical retention of all organisms >=10 um" and "6-log bacterial retention"; a 50 nm nominal pore absolutely does not retain sub-micron bacteria (typical bacteria 0.2–2 um, 100–1000x larger than 50 nm pores) by "absolute physical exclusion" — retention at that scale requires ~0.2 um pores, and 6-log retention is governed by pore-size distribution/defect population, not nominal pore size, so the causal chain (50 nm → absolute exclusion → 6-log) is physically invalid.
attacks.weak_transfer: KILLED - the testable_prediction extrapolates "linearly" 90-day TMP rise (<0.02 bar) to 12 months (<0.15 bar), but ceramic membrane fouling follows asymptotic/compressional kinetics (pore blockage + cake compression) not linear scaling; 4x longer duration over 4x the linear projection violates the specific linear-extrapolation transfer claim.
attacks.engineering_infeasibility: KILLED - 350 m3/h on 220 m2 at 26 LMH (claimed) requires 350/(220×0.026) = 61× mismatch; 350 m3/h on 220 m2 = 1590 LMH, not 26 LMH, so either flux, area, or flow is infeasible as specified.
attacks.regulatory_incompatibility: KILLED - permeate returned overboard from ballast main feed constitutes ballast discharge subject to IMO Ballast Water Management Convention D-2 biological discharge standard; a 50 nm pore cannot meet the D-2 organism size/threshold limits (which apply to organisms 10–50 um and certain indicator microbes), and "permeate-to-tank routing" for D-2 compliance requires Type Approval per the BWMS Code (IMO Resolution MEPC.300(72)), neither of which is addressed.
